title: Security claim metering and ephemeral attestation offering (pay-per-export experiment)
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Overview: Proposal for a lightweight, metered offering that lets customers request time-limited, signed security claims (ephemeral attestations) on-demand. Aims: reduce friction for small/medium enterprise procurement by providing a pay-per-export model, capture new revenue from ad-hoc evidence requests, and reduce large manual questionnaire effort. Key idea: issue a verifiable claim (signed JSON) with TTL and an auditable export event; customers pay per exported claim after a monthly free quota.

Scope: MVP covers CAIQ/SIG-style answers and a short set of signed claims (e.g., encryption-at-rest, SOC controls map, data residency statement). Backend: integrate with existing attestation store + KMS signing flow; generate signed claim artifact and short-lived download URL (expiring 24h). Billing: meter 'claim_exports' with tiered price (first 10 free / next 90 at $3/export / bulk at $1/export). UI: Console flow to request ad-hoc claim, show credits balance, and a compact evidence viewer. API: POST /claims/export -> returns claim_id, download_url, charge_id.

Hypothesis: Offering a low-friction, pay-per-export attestation will increase enterprise self-serve conversions by surfacing verifiable evidence during evaluation, reduce time-to-contract, and create incremental revenue without large manual effort from sales/SE. Success metrics: 1) 8% increase in MQL->PQL conversion in pilot accounts; 2) $X net new revenue/mo from claim_exports in first 90 days; 3) Reduction in average manual evidence turnaround time from 5 days to <24 hours for pilot customers.

Acceptance criteria: instrumented export event visible in Console usage; billing records linked to export event; signed claims verifiable by third-party (signature validation doc); UI shows credits and cost before export; automated tests for signing and TTL enforcement.

Risks & mitigations: 1) Legal/regulatory risk of signed statements -> require legal-approved claim wording and template for each claim type; prevent free-text assertions. 2) Cost to serve large exports -> cap maximum exports per account in MVP and enable bulk discount gating. 3) Abuse/spam -> enforce rate limits and require billing enabled for exports beyond free quota.

Integration notes: reuse KMS signing integration (private-key-per-org), store claim metadata in attestation-db with retention policy (90d) and audit log export hooks. Add a lightweight verification endpoint for third-parties to POST claim_id and receive signature validation result.

Deliverables: PRD, pricing table, UI mockups (Figma link), API spec (OpenAPI snippet), legal-approved claim templates, billing product change (meter + price map), pilot rollout plan, monitoring dashboard.
